title: Enolates and Carbonyl Condensations
description: α-Hydrogen acidity, aldol and Claisen reactions, enolate alkylation, and conjugate addition.
overview: The carbonyl carbon is electrophilic, but the carbon next to it, the α carbon, can be made nucleophilic. Remove an α-proton and the result is an enolate, a carbon nucleophile that attacks carbonyl compounds and alkyl halides to form carbon–carbon bonds. These reactions assemble the skeletons of sugars, steroids, fatty acids and most natural products, and they are the core of synthetic strategy.

This chapter develops enolate formation and control, then the main reactions: aldol and Claisen condensations, alkylation (including the malonic and acetoacetic ester syntheses), and conjugate addition, with ring-forming applications such as the Robinson annulation.
objectives: Explain the acidity of α-hydrogens and compare pK_a values of carbonyl compounds.
Form kinetic and thermodynamic enolates and choose bases for each.
Predict the products of aldol additions and condensations, including crossed and intramolecular versions.
Predict the products of Claisen and Dieckmann condensations.
Use malonic ester and acetoacetic ester syntheses and enamine alkylation to make substituted acids and ketones.
Describe Michael addition, 1,2- versus 1,4-addition, and the Robinson annulation.

sections.title: Enolates and α-hydrogen acidity
body: A hydrogen on the carbon next to a carbonyl is acidic, because loss of H⁺ leaves a carbanion whose charge is delocalized onto oxygen: the **enolate**. A ketone’s α-hydrogen has pK_a about 19–20, much lower than an alkane (about 50) or an alkene C–H (44).

head: Compound type
Approximate pK_a of α-H
table.caption: Acidity of α-hydrogens. A second carbonyl, between which the hydrogen sits, lowers the pK_a by about 8.

body: The base determines how much enolate forms. Hydroxide or ethoxide (conjugate acid pK_a 16–17) deprotonate a ketone only partially (an equilibrium with a small fraction of enolate), which is enough for reactions in which the enolate meets an electrophile present at the same time, as in the aldol reaction. **Lithium diisopropylamide (LDA)** (conjugate acid pK_a 36), a strong, bulky, non-nucleophilic base, converts a ketone completely to its enolate at −78 °C in THF, allowing the enolate to be made first and the electrophile added second.

An unsymmetrical ketone such as 2-methylcyclohexanone has two sets of α-hydrogens. LDA at −78 °C removes the more accessible, less substituted one, in an irreversible reaction under **kinetic control**, giving the less substituted (**kinetic**) enolate. Under equilibrating conditions (a weaker base such as NaOEt in ethanol, or higher temperature, so the enolates interconvert), the more stable, more substituted (**thermodynamic**) enolate predominates.

Under acid, a ketone enolizes slowly and brominates once at the α position. Under base the first halogen makes the remaining α-hydrogens more acidic, so reaction continues until all are replaced. A methyl ketone then undergoes the **haloform reaction**: the CX₃ group is expelled as a leaving group after hydroxide attacks the carbonyl, giving a carboxylate and CHX₃. With iodine it is the **iodoform test** (yellow precipitate of CHI₃) for methyl ketones and for CH₃CH(OH)–R. A carboxylic acid is α-brominated through its acid bromide in the **Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky** reaction (Br₂, cat. PBr₃).

example.title: Choosing the base
example.problem: Which enolate of 2-methylcyclohexanone forms with LDA at −78 °C, and which with NaOEt in EtOH?
example.solution: LDA gives the less substituted (kinetic) enolate, with the double bond toward C6, because the bulky base removes the more accessible CH₂ proton irreversibly. NaOEt allows equilibration and gives mostly the more substituted (thermodynamic) enolate, with the double bond toward the methyl-bearing carbon.

check.q: Which base gives complete, irreversible conversion of a ketone to its less substituted enolate?

sections.title: The aldol reaction
body: In the **aldol reaction** the enolate of one carbonyl compound adds to the carbonyl of another. With acetaldehyde and aqueous NaOH the product is 3-hydroxybutanal, an **aldol** (aldehyde plus alcohol):

A C–C bond forms between the α carbon of one molecule and the carbonyl carbon of the other. The step is reversible (**retro-aldol**), and ketones, with less favorable equilibria, often need the product removed. Heating the aldol product with base or acid eliminates water to give a conjugated **enone** (α,β-unsaturated carbonyl): that is the **aldol condensation**, driven by the stability of the conjugated product: CH₃CH=CHCHO (crotonaldehyde).
If two different carbonyl compounds are mixed, each can serve as enolate and as electrophile, giving up to four products. The reaction is practical in three cases:

list: One partner has **no α-hydrogens** and is a better electrophile (benzaldehyde, formaldehyde). It is added to the enolizable partner. Benzaldehyde and acetone give benzalacetone (PhCH=CHCOCH₃), a **Claisen–Schmidt** condensation, and with excess benzaldehyde, dibenzalacetone.
The enolate is made completely first with LDA (**directed aldol**), then the second carbonyl is added.
An activated methylene compound (diethyl malonate, malononitrile) condenses with aldehydes in the **Knoevenagel** condensation, catalyzed by a weak base such as piperidine.

body: A dicarbonyl compound can close a ring when five- or six-membered rings result. Hexane-2,5-dione with NaOH gives 3-methylcyclopent-2-enone.

example.title: Predict an aldol product
example.problem: Give the product of heating butanal with aqueous NaOH.
solution: The enolate of butanal (α carbon C2) attacks the carbonyl of a second butanal, giving 3-hydroxy-2-ethylhexanal.
On heating, loss of water gives the conjugated enal, 2-ethylhex-2-enal (the precursor of 2-ethylhexanol, used in plasticizers).

check.q: What drives dehydration of an aldol to the condensation product?
wrong: Formation of an aromatic ring always

check.q: Which gives a clean crossed aldol with acetone?

sections.title: Claisen and Dieckmann condensations
body: Esters also have acidic α-hydrogens (pK_a 25). In the **Claisen condensation** an ester enolate adds to the carbonyl of a second ester and, unlike an aldehyde, the tetrahedral intermediate expels alkoxide to regenerate a carbonyl: nucleophilic acyl substitution. Two molecules of ethyl acetate give ethyl acetoacetate, a **β-ketoester**:

A full equivalent of base is needed, because the product, with pK_a about 11, is deprotonated by ethoxide to a stabilized enolate. That final, favorable step pulls the otherwise unfavorable equilibrium to completion. The alkoxide must match the ester (ethoxide with ethyl esters), or ester exchange scrambles the product. A **mixed Claisen** condensation works when one ester has no α-hydrogens (ethyl benzoate, diethyl carbonate, ethyl formate).

The intramolecular version, the **Dieckmann condensation**, closes five- and six-membered rings: diethyl adipate (a 1,6-diester) gives 2-carbethoxycyclopentanone, and diethyl pimelate gives the six-membered ring analogue. Hydrolysis and decarboxylation of the β-ketoester then gives a cyclic ketone.

example.title: A Dieckmann ring closure
example.problem: What is the product of diethyl hexanedioate (diethyl adipate) with NaOEt, then H₃O⁺?
example.solution: The enolate formed at one α carbon attacks the other ester carbonyl, forming a five-membered ring and expelling ethoxide: ethyl 2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate. Treating it with aqueous acid and heat would hydrolyze the ester and decarboxylate it to cyclopentanone.

check.q: Why does the Claisen condensation need a full equivalent of base?
check.a: The product β-ketoester is deprotonated, which drives the equilibrium
wrong: The base is a catalyst that is regenerated
The ester is a weak acid
The base is consumed in making ethanol

check.a: An intramolecular Claisen condensation that forms a ring

sections.title: Alkylation of enolates
body: An enolate is a nucleophile in SN2 reactions with primary alkyl halides (methyl, primary, allylic and benzylic work best; secondary halides eliminate, and tertiary halides never work). With a ketone, LDA makes the enolate quantitatively, and the alkyl halide is then added: R–CO–CH₃ → R–CO–CH₂R′.

Diethyl malonate (pK_a 13) is converted by NaOEt entirely into its enolate and alkylated. A second alkylation is possible. Hydrolysis with aqueous acid gives a malonic acid, and heating the 1,3-diacid causes **decarboxylation**: it loses CO₂ through a cyclic six-membered transition state to give an enol, which tautomerizes. The overall result converts R–X into R–CH₂COOH, a carboxylic acid with two more carbons.

Ethyl acetoacetate (pK_a 11) is alkylated at the central carbon in the same way. Hydrolysis and decarboxylation of the β-keto acid (which loses CO₂ even more easily than a malonic acid) gives a methyl ketone, R–CH₂COCH₃. It converts R–X into a ketone with three more carbons.

example.title: Malonic ester synthesis
solution: Deprotonate diethyl malonate with NaOEt and alkylate with CH₃CH₂Br to give diethyl ethylmalonate. Deprotonate again and alkylate with CH₃I to give diethyl ethylmethylmalonate.
Hydrolyze with aqueous acid and heat: the diacid decarboxylates, leaving CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)COOH, 2-methylbutanoic acid.

example.title: Acetoacetic ester synthesis
example.solution: Alkylate the enolate of ethyl acetoacetate with benzyl bromide to give ethyl 2-benzylacetoacetate. Hydrolyze (H₃O⁺ or NaOH then H₃O⁺) and heat: decarboxylation gives PhCH₂CH₂COCH₃.

body: An enamine is a neutral, milder enolate equivalent. Its β carbon is nucleophilic and reacts with alkyl halides, acyl chlorides and Michael acceptors. Hydrolysis of the resulting iminium ion returns the ketone. This is the **Stork enamine** sequence: ketone + pyrrolidine → enamine → reaction with R–X → H₃O⁺ gives the α-alkylated ketone, with less overalkylation than with strong bases.

check.q: What is the product of the acetoacetic ester synthesis?
Which alkyl halide is unsuitable for enolate alkylation?

sections.title: Conjugate addition, Michael and Robinson reactions
body: An α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compound has two electrophilic carbons: the carbonyl carbon (C2, direct or 1,2-addition) and the β carbon (C4 of the conjugated system, **conjugate** or 1,4-addition), since resonance places partial positive charge on both. The enol or enolate that results from 1,4-addition protonates at carbon.

list: **Hard, strongly basic nucleophiles** (Grignard reagents, organolithiums, LiAlH₄) attack the carbonyl directly under kinetic control (1,2). The product is an allylic alcohol.

**Soft, weakly basic nucleophiles** (stabilized enolates, Gilman cuprates, amines, thiolates, cyanide) add 1,4, under thermodynamic control: they form a C–Nu bond at the β carbon and preserve the strong C=O bond.

body: The **Michael addition** (Michael reaction) is the 1,4-addition of an enolate (the donor) to an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl (the **Michael acceptor**), making a 1,5-dicarbonyl compound. Malonates, β-ketoesters, nitroalkanes and enamines are the usual donors.

A Michael addition followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation builds a six-membered ring in one operation: the **Robinson annulation**. Methyl vinyl ketone and a cyclohexanone enolate add 1,4 to give a 1,5-diketone, whose enolate then attacks the other ketone and dehydrates, giving a cyclohexenone fused to the first ring. It is a standard route to steroids and terpenes. With 2-methylcyclohexane-1,3-dione and methyl vinyl ketone it gives the Wieland–Miescher ketone, an intermediate for steroid synthesis.

example.title: 1,2 versus 1,4
example.problem: Predict the product of cyclohex-2-enone with (a) CH₃MgBr and (b) (CH₃)₂CuLi, each followed by H₃O⁺.
example.solution: (a) The Grignard reagent attacks the carbonyl (1,2): 1-methylcyclohex-2-en-1-ol. (b) The cuprate adds to the β carbon (1,4): 3-methylcyclohexanone.

check.q: A Gilman reagent with an enone gives…
What two reactions make up a Robinson annulation?
check.a: A Michael addition then an intramolecular aldol condensation
wrong: A Claisen and a Wittig reaction

quiz.q: Ethoxide (conjugate acid pK_a 16) is used to deprotonate acetone (pK_a 19). What is the approximate equilibrium constant for enolate formation?
quiz.why: K = 10^(pK_a of the conjugate acid of the base − pK_a of the ketone) = 10^(16 − 19) = 10⁻³. Only a small fraction of enolate forms, which suffices when an electrophile is present as in the aldol reaction.

quiz.q: The CH₂ of acetylacetone (pK_a 9) is far more acidic than the CH₃ of acetone (pK_a 19) because
quiz.a: the negative charge of the conjugate base is delocalized onto two carbonyl oxygens
wrong: the second carbonyl group is electron-donating, which weakens the C–H bond
acetylacetone forms stronger hydrogen bonds with water than acetone does
the CH₂ carbon is sp-hybridized in the diketone
quiz.why: A hydrogen between two carbonyls gives an enolate stabilized by both C=O groups. Each extra carbonyl lowers the pK_a by about 8 units.

quiz.q: 2-Methylcyclohexanone is treated with LDA in THF at −78 °C, and then CH₃I is added. The main product is
quiz.why: LDA removes the more accessible proton from the CH₂ side irreversibly, giving the kinetic enolate, and that carbon is methylated. NaOEt would allow equilibration and favor 2,2-dimethylation.

quiz.q: Acetophenone is treated with excess I₂ and NaOH. The products are
quiz.why: Base promotes repeated α-iodination of the methyl group. Hydroxide then attacks the carbonyl, and the CI₃ group leaves, giving benzoate and the yellow precipitate CHI₃.

quiz.q: Acid-catalyzed bromination of acetone stops after one bromine, whereas base-promoted bromination does not. Why?
quiz.a: In base the first Br makes the remaining α-hydrogens more acidic, so each halogenation is faster
wrong: In base the bromine is consumed by oxidizing hydroxide to hypobromite before the second step
In acid the product ketone cannot be protonated on oxygen at all, so it never enolizes again
In acid bromine adds to the carbonyl oxygen instead of the α carbon, which blocks later steps
quiz.why: The electron-withdrawing halogen stabilizes the enolate, so further deprotonation is easier under base. Under acid the halogen makes enol formation slower, so the reaction stops.

quiz.q: Propanal is heated with aqueous NaOH. The final product is
quiz.why: The α carbon (C2) of one propanal attacks the carbonyl of another, giving the aldol 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal. Heating dehydrates it to the conjugated enal. 2-Ethylhex-2-enal comes from butanal.

quiz.q: Benzaldehyde is stirred with diethyl malonate and a catalytic amount of piperidine. The product is
quiz.why: This is a Knoevenagel condensation: the activated methylene adds to the aldehyde and water is lost, giving a C=C attached to the ring. The benzyl compound would need a further reduction.

quiz.q: Ethyl acetate is treated with sodium methoxide in methanol, followed by acid. Why is this a poor choice of base for a Claisen condensation?
wrong: diethyl benzylmalonate, PhCH₂CH(CO₂Et)₂, from simple alkylation of the malonate
benzoic acid and diethyl malonate, from oxidation of the aldehyde by the base
ethyl 3-oxo-3-phenylpropanoate, PhCOCH₂CO₂Et, from a Claisen-type acylation
quiz.why: The alkoxide should match the ester so that nucleophilic substitution at the carbonyl returns the same ester. Otherwise transesterification scrambles the alkoxy groups.

quiz.q: Ethyl benzoate and ethyl acetate react with NaOEt, followed by acid. The main crossed Claisen product is
quiz.why: Ethyl benzoate has no α-hydrogens, so it can only be the electrophile. The ethyl acetate enolate attacks it and ethoxide is expelled, giving PhCOCH₂CO₂Et.

quiz.q: Diethyl heptanedioate (diethyl pimelate) is treated with NaOEt, and the product is then heated with aqueous acid. The final product is
quiz.why: Dieckmann closure forms a six-membered β-ketoester ring. Hydrolysis and decarboxylation of the β-keto acid then removes the ester carbon as CO₂, leaving the ring ketone.

quiz.q: Which alkyl halide is used with diethyl malonate (then hydrolysis and heat) to prepare 4-phenylbutanoic acid?
quiz.why: The malonic ester synthesis gives R–CH₂COOH. For PhCH₂CH₂CH₂COOH, R is PhCH₂CH₂. Benzyl bromide would give 3-phenylpropanoic acid, and an aryl halide does not undergo SN2.

quiz.q: Why do β-keto acids and malonic acids lose CO₂ on gentle heating, whereas simple carboxylic acids do not?
quiz.a: A cyclic six-membered transition state lets the second carbonyl accept electrons, giving an enol
wrong: They are much stronger acids, so the carboxylate is a good leaving group for CO₂ loss
The extra carbonyl oxidizes the carboxyl carbon to CO₂ when the compound is warmed
They are deprotonated to carbanions that eject CO₂ directly at room temperature
quiz.why: The carboxyl O–H hydrogen-bonds to the β carbonyl, and the cyclic arrangement allows C–C cleavage with formation of an enol, which tautomerizes. A simple acid has no such acceptor.

quiz.q: Ethyl acetoacetate is alkylated with 1-bromobutane. Hydrolysis and heating then give
quiz.why: The acetoacetic ester synthesis adds three carbons (CH₂COCH₃) to R, so butyl gives CH₃COCH₂C₄H₉, heptan-2-one. Hexanoic acid is what malonic ester gives with the same halide.

quiz.q: In the Stork enamine alkylation of cyclohexanone with CH₃I via its pyrrolidine enamine, which atom of the enamine attacks the alkyl halide productively?
quiz.a: The carbon β to the nitrogen, which was the α carbon of the ketone
wrong: The nitrogen, which gives a stable quaternary salt that hydrolyzes to the product
The carbon bonded to nitrogen, which carries the positive charge
A CH₂ of the pyrrolidine ring
quiz.why: The nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the C=C, which makes the β carbon nucleophilic. Hydrolysis of the resulting iminium ion returns the α-alkylated ketone.

quiz.q: The Michael addition of diethyl malonate to methyl vinyl ketone gives a
quiz.why: The malonate carbon adds to the β carbon of the enone, which is two carbons from the ketone carbonyl. The new chain separates the two carbonyls by three carbons, making them 1,5-related.

quiz.q: The new ring built in a Robinson annulation is
wrong: a six-membered ring with a β-hydroxy ketone, since no dehydration occurs
quiz.why: The Michael adduct (a 1,5-diketone) closes by intramolecular aldol, and loss of water gives the conjugated cyclohexenone fused to the original ring.

quiz.q: Cyclohex-2-enone is treated with phenyllithium, and then H₃O⁺ is added. The product is
quiz.why: Organolithiums are hard, strongly basic nucleophiles that attack the carbonyl carbon directly under kinetic control (1,2). A cuprate would give the 1,4 product, 3-phenylcyclohexanone.

summary: α-Hydrogens are acidic (pK_a 17–25 for simple carbonyls, 9–13 for 1,3-dicarbonyls). LDA gives the kinetic enolate completely, and NaOEt gives the thermodynamic one under equilibrium.
Aldol reactions join an enolate and a carbonyl. Heat gives the enone (condensation). Crossed aldols work when one partner has no α-H.
Claisen condensations of esters give β-ketoesters and are driven by deprotonation of the product. Dieckmann closes 5- and 6-membered rings.
Enolate alkylation requires primary halides. Malonic ester synthesis gives substituted acetic acids, and acetoacetic ester gives methyl ketones, after decarboxylation.
Soft nucleophiles add 1,4 to enones and hard ones add 1,2. Michael addition plus aldol is the Robinson annulation.

problems.q: Give the products: (a) cyclohexanone + LDA (−78 °C), then CH₃I; (b) benzaldehyde + acetophenone + NaOH, heat; (c) ethyl propanoate + NaOEt, then H₃O⁺.
problems.solution: (a) 2-Methylcyclohexanone. (b) Chalcone, PhCH=CHCOPh. (c) Ethyl 2-methyl-3-oxopentanoate (CH₃CH₂COCH(CH₃)COOEt), the Claisen product.

problems.q: Outline a synthesis of hexanoic acid from diethyl malonate.
problems.solution: Deprotonate diethyl malonate with NaOEt and alkylate once with 1-bromobutane to give diethyl butylmalonate. Hydrolyze with aqueous acid and heat; decarboxylation gives CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂COOH, hexanoic acid (the butyl group plus two carbons from malonate).

problems.q: Show how an intramolecular aldol converts heptane-2,6-dione into 3-methylcyclohex-2-enone.
problems.solution: Base removes an α-hydrogen from C1 (the methyl) to give an enolate, which attacks the carbonyl at C6 through a six-membered ring transition state. Dehydration of the β-hydroxy ketone forms the conjugated enone, a six-membered ring with the methyl group of the other end at C3.
problems.a: Enolate attack on the C6 carbonyl, then dehydration.

problems.q: Why does a secondary alkyl halide give poor yields in the malonic ester synthesis?
problems.solution: The enolate is also a base. With a secondary halide, SN2 is slow and E2 elimination competes, giving an alkene from the halide.
